explanation: Maintain a max-heap for the lower half and a min-heap for the upper half. Balance their sizes so the lower half has at most one extra entry. The median is its maximum, or the average of both heap roots.
timeComplexity: O(n log n) Each of n inputs makes a constant number of heap operations on at most n entries.
spaceComplexity: O(n), excluding output Both heaps together hold all n observed values; output has n medians.
attribution: Original C++ implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from its public native contract and repository-authored C# algorithm. Existing upstream reference files remain unchanged.
correctness: The lower heap contains the lower half and upper contains the upper half; every lower entry is no greater than every upper entry. Rebalancing preserves that ordering and keeps lower the same size or one larger. Hence its maximum is the odd-length median, while the two roots are the even-length middle values.
walkthrough: For stream [9,1,5,3], prefix medians are 9, (1+9)/2=5, 5 and (3+5)/2=4. Return [9,5,5,4].
edgeCases: The first entry is its own median.
Even prefixes require an average rather than either middle entry alone.
Widening the middle-value sum prevents int overflow.
